description: The non-framebuffer gates. Two kinds live here. 'savestate' runs --diag-savestate-roundtrip and IS gated: it compares a continuously-played NES against an identical one that did a SaveState+LoadState round trip mid-play, frame by frame, and fails if any state the savestate is responsible for came back different. (A framebuffer-only immediate difference is expected and benign - the framebuffer is a render target, not machine state - and that is why the verdict string below says so; the false failure that used to come from treating it as a fault was fixed on 2026-09-02.) 'benchmark' runs --benchmark and is INFORMATIONAL ONLY: timing is machine-dependent, so it is printed and never affects the exit code.

cases.description: Savestate round trip on a bundled story ROM with the accuracy-target cores.
Same round trip on the FMC family, so a serialisation regression in one family cannot hide behind the other.
A second story ROM, so the savestate gate is not a property of one ROM.
Savestate round trip on MMC3/SMB3 - mapper bank state and scanline-IRQ counters are the parts of a savestate most likely to be forgotten. SKIPs when the 65-o-borked corpus is not on the machine.

INFORMATIONAL. Speed of the accuracy-target stack. Never gates. Its point is the FIX-vs-FMC delta on the line below: the project policy is that an accuracy fix which meaningfully regresses speed for marginal gain should be rejected, and this row is how you notice.
INFORMATIONAL. Same ROM on FMC, as the speed reference point FIX is judged against.
INFORMATIONAL. The speed-oriented SPD family, as the upper bound of what these cores can do on this machine.
